answer: An answer must include the first 21 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake. Because the ivory derivation is checked against the quill nonce, the relic audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 59 aliases produces 59 mismatches and pays the authoring cost with no payout. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
